body.name: \widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)
body.construction: This is the evaluable \(\kappa=0\) second-order attainer.  Let \(v\) be a fixed Lebesgue-orthonormal polynomial basis through degree \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\) on \(D=[0,1]^d\).  With \(M=M_0+\lfloor k^{1/d}\rfloor\), let \(b_k\) be the explicit cellwise scaled-Legendre basis of degree \(p=\lceil\gamma\rceil-1+\max\{\lceil\alpha\rceil-1,\lceil\beta\rceil-1\}\), whose exact Gram matrix is \(\Omega_M=I\).  Put \(w_h(x)=h^{-d}{\bf1}_{hD}(x)\), \(v_h(x)=v(x/h){\bf1}_{hD}(x)\), \(b_{h,k}(x)=b_k(x/h){\bf1}_{hD}(x)\), and use fixed pilots \(\bar e=3/8,\bar\mu=1/2\).  For \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_if(O_i)\) and ordered \(\mathbb U_nH=[n(n-1)]^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}H(O_i,O_j)\), define \(\phi_{a1}=A(A-\bar e),\ \phi_{y1}=(Y-\bar\mu)(A-\bar e)\), \(\phi_{a2}(O_1,O_2)=-(A_1-\bar e)b_{h,k}(X_1)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(X_2)A_2\), and \(\phi_{y2}(O_1,O_2)=-(A_1-\bar e)b_{h,k}(X_1)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(X_2)(Y_2-\bar\mu)\).  Set \(\widetilde Q=\mathbb P_n[w_hv_h\phi_{a1}v_h^{\mathsf T}]+\mathbb U_n[w_h(X_1)w_h(X_2)v_h(X_1)\phi_{a2}v_h(X_2)^{\mathsf T}]\) and \(\widetilde R=\mathbb P_n[w_hv_h\phi_{y1}]+\mathbb U_n[w_h(X_1)w_h(X_2)v_h(X_1)\phi_{y2}]\).  If \(\widetilde Q=U\operatorname{diag}(s_j)V^{\mathsf T}\) is the deterministic Borel SVD specified by lexicographic tie breaking, set \(\widetilde Q_{\rm fl}=U\operatorname{diag}(s_j\vee3/32)V^{\mathsf T}\) and output \(\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}[v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_{\rm fl}^{-1}\widetilde R]\).  Thus the map uses finite sample moments and finite matrix operations and is total even if the localization cube is empty.  For \(S=\alpha+\beta\), use \(h_n=n^{-1/(\gamma D_\star)},\ k_n\asymp n^{(d/S-d/\gamma)/D_\star}\) when \(S<S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(h_n=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},\ k_n\asymp nh_n^d\) when \(S\ge S_\star\), with the displayed bounded-ratio integer rounding; these are deterministic functions of the known parameters.
